Advanced techniques identified iron-containing heme and collagen, suggesting biological materials survived long periods. Researchers believe rapid burial in low-oxygen conditions contributed to preservation. This discovery opens new avenues for understanding dinosaur biology beyond skeletal re…

items.title: Ancient Spanish copper mine hints at Bronze Age trade with Scandinavia
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Archaeologists conducted a thorough investigation of Las Minillas, an ancient copper mine in southern Spain, revealing its historical impact. Over 700 stone tools and pottery shards were found, pinpointing extensive activity from 1300 to 700 BC. This research indicates that the copper mined here likely reached Scandinavia through trade networks, showcasing the interconnectedness of Bronze Age communities across Europe.

items.title: Sebi allows AIF managers to determine investor accreditation status for simplified processes
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced a new regulation allowing alternative investment fund managers to handle investor accreditation. This initiative is designed to streamline the accreditation process for investors looking for investment options. Managers are now authorized to evaluate eligibility during onboarding or at any stage of the scheme, providing greater flexibility.

items.title: Sebi relaxes cash market settlement rules for mutual funds
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has permitted mutual fund schemes to net fund obligations. This new regulation is set to come into effect starting April 1, 2027. It allows net settlement of funds at the individual scheme level while maintaining gross settlement for securities. Fund obligations cannot be adjusted across different schemes, and inter-scheme funding remains prohibited. Proceeds from outright sales must be funded separately for non-outright obligations.

items.title: Julia Child's former home sells for $6.525m; famous kitchen now in museum
items.author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
items.description: Julia Child’s iconic home in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has found a new owner for $6.525 million. This historic residence, adored for its connection to Child's culinary shows, has seen extensive renovations. The original kitchen, however, remains untouched and is now a cherished exhibit at the Smithsonian Museum. To honor her legacy, a commemorative plaque is set to be installed at the site, ensuring that Child's influence on cooking continues.

Successful initiatives may help restore these vital habitats for future generations.

items.title: Georgia waste plant permit upheld despite developer's plan for 97 townhomes
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A developer in Bartow County, Georgia challenged a permit for a nearby waste processing facility. The county approved the permit despite concerns that it violated zoning restrictions. The developer argued that their planned townhomes should receive protection under existing zoning laws. Ultimately, the appeals court upheld the permit, allowing the waste facility to operate.

items.title: Psychology says avoiding someone you know in public isn't always social anxiety

items.description: Many individuals choose to avoid eye contact with familiar faces in public spaces to evade unforeseen interactions. items.title: NASA's Hubble probes mystery of missing oxygen in dwarf galaxies
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: A recent investigation revealed that dwarf galaxies only retain an average of 11% of the oxygen generated by their stars. The remaining oxygen likely escapes into space during powerful supernova explosions. This finding indicates that smaller galaxies have greater difficulty retaining their materials than previously believed. Researchers plan to conduct further studies to examine where this missing oxygen ultimately ends up.
